title: IR blaster fires but fan does not respond -- stepped diagnostic
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)
Every check reachable from a keyboard is done and the fault is now isolated to
something only hands, eyes, or a second part can test:
1. Content: the blaster's self-capture of `0xD81` is bit-identical to the real
   remote (Step 1 done). 2. Delivery: 42/42 presses reached the device, and a
   power cycle changed nothing. 3. Framing: the `PROBE carrier 0Hz` / `20kHz`
   buttons (live at http://192.168.0.6/) only exclude TOTAL carrier loss — the
   5990's own receiver decodes an 18 kHz-off carrier 2/3 of the time at 2 in, so
   it cannot measure carrier depth. The live hypothesis is a degraded emitter
   drive path (weak 38 kHz on a DC pedestal): decodes up close, starves the fan
   across the room. No firmware change can measure or fix that. Re-verified
   2026-08-30 without touching hardware: ping 0% loss, web 200, uptime 11.95 d,
   all four buttons present; nothing has changed on the device side.

## Steps
Cheapest first. The fan is a TOGGLE: success = it CHANGES state. Fire from
http://192.168.0.6/ (`Fan Power`) to keep the watch/HA chain out of the loop.
1. **Reseat (free, 5 min — Step 3).** Pull and re-push all four 4045 leads on
   the breadboard, especially red (VIN→3V) and green (IRout→GPIO27); pinch the
   tinned tips. Fire `Fan Power`. Toggled → soldering the four leads to the
   Feather is the permanent fix (no firmware change); close this issue.
2. **Proximity (Step 4).** Hold the blaster 1–2 ft from the fan's receiver,
   fire. Works close but not from its spot → range/amplitude confirmed. Fails
   at 1 ft → not range.
3. **Swap the emitter (tests the live hypothesis).** Fit a second Adafruit 5990
   (BOM row 1, docs/hardware.md) — same 4 leads, VIN to **3V**, IRout GPIO27,
   IRin GPIO14. Fire. Toggled → old 5990 is degraded; mark it so it is not
   reused as the TX part in `ir-sniffer-blaster-exg`. (A second 5990 also
   unblocks that spike's TX leg, which needs a witness receiver.)
4. **Only if 1–3 all fail (Step 2 / carrier depth).** Dark room, phone camera:
   remote vs blaster at ~6 in, both emitters (one vertical, one horizontal).
   Comparable brightness with no actuation means a scope/photodiode on the
   green line is the next measurement — that is beyond this repo's tooling.
5. Record which step changed the fan state in this issue, then close it.

Branch note (decision for you, not done by the agent): the regression docs and
the probe buttons that are flashed to the production device live on
`esp8266-uno-wifi-spike` (11 commits ahead of `main`). `main`'s README/AGENTS
still say the blaster works. Merge or cherry-pick when you are ready.

## What unblocks me when this returns
A one-line note here saying which step toggled the fan (or that none did and
what the camera/scope showed). If a part swap fixed it, say so and I will
update docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/hardware.md (add "5990 emitter degraded
after ~9 days at 3V VIN" to the range note) and validation.md's R1/R15 rows.

---
## Prior diagnostic record (unchanged, kept verbatim)
Fan stopped responding to the blaster on the night of 2026-08-17 (first bad
window 2026-08-18T03:48Z = 23:48 local, 5 presses in 40s). Watch reports
RELAYED / "relay: empty reply", which is the app's SUCCESS state, not an error.

ESTABLISHED 2026-08-18 -- do NOT retest:
- Fan is powered and works via the real remote (owner).
- Real remote works FROM THE BLASTER'S POSITION, so room geometry, line of
  sight and the fan's IR receiver are all fine (owner).
- Blaster's IR LED visibly emits (owner).
- Watch -> phone -> webhook -> automation -> button.press measured working:
  automation.bangle_ir_blaster_fan_power last_triggered 2026-08-18T13:24:05Z,
  context user_id null (webhook-originated).
- Blaster online at 192.168.0.6: ping 0% loss, TCP 6053 open, web_server 200.
  Uptime 664408s = 7.69d, so no reboot since the 2026-08-10 bedroom move.
- Blaster transmits and self-decodes as Symphony data=0xD81 nbits=12. Two
  captures ~5 min apart match in structure (24 burst pairs) within +/-2 units
  of jitter, so transmission is stable and repeatable.
- HA-side artefacts CANNOT prove actuation (validation.md R15): ESPHome buttons
  are stateless, button.* state is HA's local last_pressed, and
  automation.last_triggered only says the automation started.

DEGRADATION PATTERN (button.* history): single presses 08-11..08-14, then 4
presses on 08-15, 2 on 08-16, single on 08-17, then 5 in 40s on 08-18 03:48Z
and nothing since. Progressive decay, not a step change.

REMAINING UNKNOWNS: content (does the pattern match the real remote), amplitude
(does it carry across the room), framing (carrier / duty / command_repeats).
Carrier is NOT measurable from our captures -- the 5990 hands ESPHome a
demodulated signal, so the 006D in the pronto header is the dumper's assumption.

TOGGLE SEMANTICS: Fan Power is a toggle and the fan is currently ON, so success
in every step below is the fan CHANGING STATE, not "turning on".

FAST TRIGGER for iteration: http://192.168.0.6/ (ESPHome web UI) has both
buttons; this cuts watch/phone/Gadgetbridge/webhook/HA out of the loop.

STEP 1 -- CONTENT. Capture the real remote on the blaster's own receiver and
diff against the blaster's self-capture. Stored code was captured 2026-08-09,
BEFORE the 08-10 move to the bedroom. Differ -> flash the captured code, done.
Identical -> content eliminated, go to Step 2.

STEP 2 -- AMPLITUDE (no wiring touched). Dark room, phone camera. Compare real
remote LED vs blaster LED at the same ~6in. Check BOTH 5990 emitters (one
vertical, one horizontal). Dimmer / only one lit -> Step 3. Comparable -> Step 5.
Context: VIN is deliberately at 3V not 5V (pin-safe receiver line), and
docs/hardware.md states this "caps emitter range".

STEP 3 -- CONNECTIONS. Reseat all four 4045 leads, esp. red (VIN/3V) and green
(IRout/GPIO27). Pinch tinned tips. docs/wiring.md: "The breadboard is the least
rugged link for a permanent fixture." Fits the 3-day decay. Permanent fix is
soldering the four leads to the Feather; no firmware change.

STEP 4 -- PROXIMITY. Only if 2 and 3 inconclusive. Move blaster to within 1-2ft
of the fan's receiver, repower, fire. Works close but not at normal spot ->
range problem (reorient board to the other emitter LED, or drive a separate 5V
emitter). Fails at 1ft -> Step 5. CAVEAT: moving disturbs the breadboard, so a
fix after moving may be Step 3's reseat rather than proximity -- hence 3 first.

STEP 5 -- FRAMING. Fire the Symphony probe button (decoded form, state unknown,
never pressed since it was added 2026-08-09). If that also fails, OTA variant
buttons: command_repeats above the default 2, and carrier at 36kHz and 40kHz.

STEP 6 -- RECEIVER STATE. Only if 1-5 pass. Press blaster, then immediately try
the real remote. If the remote also stops working briefly, the blaster is
jamming/confusing the receiver rather than failing to reach it.

RULED OUT: the off-network watch press. The watch URL is a bare LAN IP
(192.168.0.70), so off-LAN it times out at the phone and never reaches HA -- no
trace, no state. Automation is mode:single with current:0 (nothing stuck), the
ESP32 never rebooted, and the watch app is stateless between taps with a 10s
watchdog. Nothing carries forward.

notes:
SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-18 (roborev #3925, Medium).

Earlier notes on this issue said flatly 'CARRIER LOSS IS RULED OUT' and listed
AMPLITUDE among the eliminated items. Both are OVERSTATED and are corrected
here, because that unscoped wording propagated out of this issue into
docs/troubleshooting.md and steered readers away from the live hypothesis.

WHAT THE 0 Hz PROBE ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED: only that a FULLY unmodulated
emitter is excluded -- the LED is not simply held DC-on through each mark.
Nothing more. The 20 kHz row proves this receiver CANNOT discriminate carrier
quality: at ~2 in it decoded a carrier 18 kHz off target 2/3 of the time.

STILL LIVE: a DEGRADED emitter drive path -- a weak 38 kHz component riding on
a large DC pedestal. It would decode at 2 in, look brighter than the remote on
a camera (100% vs 50% duty), and still starve the fan at distance. Measuring
carrier depth needs a scope or a photodiode, not this board.

ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT (unchanged): code content (bit-identical envelope to
the real remote), aim, delivery reliability (42/42), repeat count, runtime
state (power cycle).
NOT ELIMINATED: carrier depth / emitter-drive amplitude at distance.

Consequence for the part decision: replacing the 5990 tests a LIVE hypothesis,
not merely the last unverified component.
2026-08-30 agent sweep: gates green (23/23 unit, all 4 ESPHome configs validate), blaster re-verified online (uptime 11.95d, 4 buttons live). Nothing agent-side remains; handed to human at Step 3 (reseat) with 5990 swap as the hypothesis test.

title: Sniff the fan remote's speed-up and speed-down codes; add transmit_symphony buttons
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)

The watch fan app is gaining SPEED - and SPEED + next to FAN POWER
(`my-bangle-450`, code landed 2026-09-01). That needs two more IR codes off
the fan remote, and capturing them is physical: someone has to hold the
remote in front of the blaster and press the buttons.

**Everything except the button press is verified working as of 2026-09-01**,
so this is a five-minute job, not a setup session:

- `esphome` 2026.6.2 is already installed in `.venv` (it is NOT on `$PATH` —
  use `.venv/bin/esphome`)
- the board is **online and reachable from this Mac**. `esphome logs`
  connected over the encrypted API and printed a full boot dump: receiver on
  GPIO14, transmitter on GPIO27, WiFi signal -66 dB
- `esphome config` validates clean
- the protocol is already known. With `inverted: true` this remote decodes as
  **Symphony `data=0xD81`, `nbits=12`** — it is not the "UNKNOWN protocol" the
  project was originally built around, that was a polarity artefact. So each
  new button is ~3 fields of YAML, not a 120-entry raw timing array

**Address note:** the board moved from `192.168.0.6` to `192.168.0.3` (it has
no DHCP reservation — `home-assistant-pi-6sf`). Use the mDNS name, which is
what the command below resolves by default. HA had already followed the move
on its own; nothing is broken.

The one thing I cannot rule out from here is what the remote actually has on
it — see step 2.

## Steps

1. From `~/Projects/personal/ir-sniffer-blaster`, start the log stream:

   ```
   .venv/bin/esphome logs ir-blaster-livingroom.yaml
   ```

   Wait for the boot dump to finish so you know it is connected.

2. Look at the remote before pressing anything. Does it have a **discrete
   speed-up and speed-down**, or **one speed button that cycles**? Note which
   here — it decides whether the watch gets one speed cell or two.

3. Point the remote at the board and press **speed up** slowly, **at least 3
   times**, pausing between presses. Each press should log:

   ```
   [I][remote.symphony:117]: Received Symphony: data=0x???, nbits=12
   ```

4. Same for **speed down**, at least 3 times.

5. Check each button's value **repeats across its presses**. A value that
   changes every press is a rolling code and cannot be replayed — say so here
   and stop; the feature is not possible with this remote. Fan power gave 28
   identical captures, so this is unlikely.

6. Paste the captured lines into this issue, or straight into
   `captured-codes/README.md` as one table row per button, matching the
   existing `fan-power-switch` row.

7. Close this issue when complete.

## What unblocks me when this returns

Two Symphony data values, one per button, each confirmed stable over 3+
presses — plus the answer to step 2.

With those I add the two `transmit_symphony` template buttons and OTA-flash
the board (OTA is proven; no USB needed), then `home-assistant-pi-51o` can
name the resulting entity ids and `my-bangle-7nc` can be deployed to the
watch. Nothing else in the chain is blocked on hardware.

## Prior description (preserved on handoff)

The Bangle.js watch app is gaining SPEED - and SPEED + alongside FAN POWER (my-bangle-450 / my-bangle-7nc). That needs two more codes off the same remote.

Why this should be easy: the remote is NOT an unknown protocol. With inverted: true the receiver decodes fan power as Symphony data=0xD81, nbits=12, and the raw and decoded forms are the same signal on the RX side. So each new button is ~3 fields, not a 120-entry raw array.

Capture (physical, needs the remote and the board in the same room):
  esphome logs ir-blaster-livingroom.yaml
  press SPEED UP a few times, then SPEED DOWN a few times
  read 'Received Symphony: data=0x..., nbits=12' out of the log

Record in captured-codes/README.md, one row per button. Press each at least 3x and confirm the value repeats -- a value that changes every press is a rolling code and cannot be replayed. Fan power gave 28 identical captures, so this remote is very unlikely to roll.

Then add two template buttons beside the existing 'Fan Power' one, transmit_symphony with the captured data and nbits: 12. Leave command_repeats at its default 2 -- that is what the real remote does. OTA flash; USB is not needed (proven).

Open question worth answering while the remote is in hand: are speed up/down discrete codes, or does the remote send one 'speed' code that cycles? If it cycles, the watch gets one SPEED cell instead of two and my-bangle-7nc's layout changes.
close_reason:
Done 2026-09-02. Codes captured, shipped as raw buttons, OTA-flashed, and direction confirmed on the running fan.

  speed UP   = Symphony 0xD82
  speed DOWN = Symphony 0xD92

Both stable over 5 presses, neither rolling. The remote has discrete up/down, not one cycling button, so my-bangle's two-cell watch layout stands.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE CODES:

1. The direction is INVERTED relative to the remote button that produced each code. The owner pressed increase first (giving 0xD92), but firing 0xD92 steps the fan DOWN. Actuation beats a report of which button was pressed. The yaml anchors are now named by code (&sym_d82_raw), never by direction, so there is exactly one place the direction is asserted.

2. A run into a powered-off fan is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a dead emitter. Seven presses with the fan off gave HTTP 200 on all seven and correct self-decodes on the board, and the fan did nothing -- which reads exactly like ir-sniffer-blaster-54y. The owner does not leave the fan running between tests; every future sitting must open with a Fan Power press confirmed by a human.

Also measured: both ends clamp, neither code wraps, so SPEED + at max does nothing rather than dumping to minimum. Inferred (not measured): ~4 speed levels.

Symphony TX probes for both new codes ship alongside the raw buttons, so the open probe question can now be settled on any of three codes. Next: home-assistant-pi-51o, then the watch deploy on my-bangle-7jp.

title: Spike: prove the UNO+WiFi R3 (ESP8266) can run the IR sniffer/blaster role
description:
## Why this needs you (please confirm this is accurate)
The firmware side of the spike is finished and verified: `uno-wifi-test.yaml`
validates against ESPHome 2026.6.2 (re-checked 2026-08-30), it flashes and
boots on the HW-649 (DIP 5,6,7 to flash; 5,6 for logs), and the 15 s
`TX beacon: Symphony 0x5A5` line fires. What is left is entirely physical:
(1) the 5990 has to be wired to the ESP8266 headers, and the only 5990 in the
BOM is on the production Feather; (2) the RX leg needs the real remote pressed
at it; (3) the TX leg needs a SECOND receiver as witness because the ESP8266
cannot hear its own transmission (bit-banged TX under InterruptLock masks the
RX ISR — remote_transmitter.cpp:86-103) — and both witness configs
(`ir-wiring-test.yaml`, the prod device's `dump: all`) also need a 5990. With
one transceiver the TX leg cannot be witnessed at all.

## Steps
1. **Get a second 5990** (Adafruit IR transceiver; docs/hardware.md BOM row 1).
   This is the same part `ir-sniffer-blaster-54y` step 3 wants, so one order
   serves both. Alternative if you would rather not buy: temporarily move the
   prod 5990 to the UNO for the RX leg only, and accept that the TX leg stays
   unproven.
2. **Wire the 5990 to the HW-649 ESP8266 headers** (uno-wifi-test.yaml header):
   red → **3.3V** (mandatory — no 5V-tolerant pins on ESP8266), black → GND,
   white (IRin) → GPIO5, green (IRout) → GPIO4. DIP switches 1-4 OFF always.
3. **RX leg.** DIP 5,6 ON; `.venv/bin/esphome logs uno-wifi-test.yaml`. Point
   the real fan remote at the 5990, press. PASS = `Received Symphony:
   data=0xD81, nbits=12`. Silent → swap white/green (many boards silkscreen
   GPIO4/5 swapped) before debugging anything else.
4. **TX leg.** Point the UNO's 5990 at the witness: the prod blaster
   (`.venv/bin/esphome logs ir-blaster-livingroom.yaml`, dump: all) or the
   Feather on `ir-wiring-test.yaml`. PASS = witness logs Symphony `0x5A5`
   every 15 s. (0x5A5 is deliberately not the fan's code; it actuates nothing.)
5. Paste both log excerpts (or the failing leg) into this issue and close it,
   or note the failure and leave it open for the agent.

## What unblocks me when this returns
The two PASS log lines (or which leg failed and what the log showed) recorded
on this issue. With a two-leg PASS I will write the go/no-go section in the
docs and file the follow-up R1-style gate (wifi enabled, real 0xD81 against
the fan) that decides whether this board can take the enclosed-build role.

---
## Prior description (unchanged, kept verbatim)
Owner has a UNO+WiFi R3 ATmega328P+ESP8266 CH340 (4MB flash ESP8266, external antenna) sitting around; if its ESP8266 half can run ESPHome remote_receiver/remote_transmitter, it becomes a candidate for the enclosed (Altoids tin) build where the Feather's PCB antenna dies. All ESP8266 pins are broken out on female headers (owner confirmed). Isolated on branch esp8266-uno-wifi-spike; main untouched. Test vehicle: uno-wifi-test.yaml — no wifi/api/ota/secrets, serial-only, GPIO5 RX / GPIO4 TX (only two non-strap interrupt-capable pins), and an every-15s Symphony loopback self-test using data=0x5A5 (deliberately NOT the fan's 0xD81) so it can never actuate the living-room fan. Pass = log shows the transmitted code decoded by the device's own receiver, mirroring the loopback behavior proven on the Feather 2026-08-09. ESP8266 caveat: bit-banged IR (no RMT), so this spike proves capability, not equivalence — an R1-style gate on real hardware still applies before trusting it.

## Prior description (preserved on handoff)

Owner has a UNO+WiFi R3 ATmega328P+ESP8266 CH340 (4MB flash ESP8266, external antenna) sitting around; if its ESP8266 half can run ESPHome remote_receiver/remote_transmitter, it becomes a candidate for the enclosed (Altoids tin) build where the Feather's PCB antenna dies. All ESP8266 pins are broken out on female headers (owner confirmed). Isolated on branch esp8266-uno-wifi-spike; main untouched. Test vehicle: uno-wifi-test.yaml — no wifi/api/ota/secrets, serial-only, GPIO5 RX / GPIO4 TX (only two non-strap interrupt-capable pins), and an every-15s Symphony loopback self-test using data=0x5A5 (deliberately NOT the fan's 0xD81) so it can never actuate the living-room fan. Pass = log shows the transmitted code decoded by the device's own receiver, mirroring the loopback behavior proven on the Feather 2026-08-09. ESP8266 caveat: bit-banged IR (no RMT), so this spike proves capability, not equivalence — an R1-style gate on real hardware still applies before trusting it.
notes:
CORRECTION (roborev 3445, HIGH, verified in vendored source): on-device loopback is impossible on ESP8266 — remote_transmitter bit-bangs under InterruptLock (remote_transmitter.cpp:86-103) while remote_receiver captures via GPIO ISR (remote_receiver.cpp:74), so the device cannot hear its own TX. Test restructured to two legs: RX = point real fan remote at 5990, expect Received Symphony 0xD81; TX = 0x5A5 beacon every 15s, witnessed by a second receiver (Feather on ir-wiring-test.yaml or the prod living-room device's dump: all). Status: firmware flashed and booting on the HW-649 (DIP switches were hidden under factory kapton film; 5,6,7 to flash, 5,6 for logs); TX beacon confirmed firing in logs. Awaiting 5990 rewire + two-leg verification.
2026-08-30 agent sweep: uno-wifi-test.yaml re-validated. Blocked on physical 5990 wiring + second receiver as TX witness; handed to human.
